properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents and breaking waves due to
elevated surf up to 4 to 6 feet expected. Minor tidal overflow
possible during morning high tides, especially across west
facing beaches.

* WHERE...Santa Barbara County Southwestern Coast and Santa
Barbara County Southeastern Coast.

* WHEN...Through Tuesday morning.

* IMPACTS...There is an increased risk of ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can
wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats
nearshore. Pooling of sea water is possible around high tide
at beach and harbor areas that is uncommon with normal tidal
ranges. Enhanced beach erosion is also possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides of 7.2 to 7.4 feet (MLLW) are
expected each morning.
properties.instruction:
Remain out of the water due to hazardous swimming conditions, or
stay near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly
in such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued November 9 at 11:55AM AKST until November 11 at 6:00AM AKST by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Snow and blowing snow expected. Total snow accumulations up
to three inches. Winds gusting as high as 55 mph.

* WHERE...Portions of the Central Arctic Coast & Northwest Arctic
Coast.

* WHEN...From 9 PM this evening to 6 AM AKST Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. Areas of blowing snow
could reduce visibility to around 1/2 mile at times. Blizzard
conditions will be intermittently possible to the east of
Utqiagvik, which will be dependent on the severity of blowing snow
& intensity of the snowfall.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Scattered light snow showers are expected to
continue during this timeframe. Steadier snowfall along with
heavier snowfall rates are expected to start early Tuesday morning
& last through Tuesday. East-northeast winds will increase as we
progress into Tuesday & generally remain elevated through midweek.
Areas to the east of Utqiagvik could intermittently experience
visibilities as low as 1/4 mile from the onset of the snowfall from
around early Tuesday morning into Tuesday evening as both the
snowfall rates & the wind gusts will be higher over that area
during that timeframe.

two inches. Winds gusting as high as 55 mph.

* WHERE...Central Beaufort Sea Coast & Eastern Beaufort Sea Coast.

* WHEN...From 9 PM this evening to 6 AM AKST Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult at times. Areas of blowing
snow will significantly reduce visibility. Strong winds could
result in some power outages. Visibilities dropping to as low as
1/4 mile or less are expected at times, resulting in blizzard
conditions, depending on the intensity of the falling snow & the
severity of the blowing snow.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...East-northeast winds will increase as we
progress into Tuesday & generally remain elevated through midweek.
Scattered light snow showers are expected to continue during this
timeframe with the blizzard conditions most likely to start along
with the onset of steadier snowfall & heavier snowfall rates, which
will occur from late tonight through Tuesday & last through Tuesday
night.
properties.instruction:
A Blizzard Warning means severe winter weather conditions are
expected or occurring. Falling and blowing snow with strong winds are
likely. This will lead to whiteout conditions, making travel
extremely dangerous. If you must travel, have a winter survival kit
with you. If you get stranded, stay in your vehicle.

properties.instruction:
There is a high risk of rip currents.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.

* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Beaches of Volusia, Indian River, Saint Lucie, Martin,
and Brevard Counties.

* WHEN...Through late Monday night.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.
